editorial: Sri Lanka has distinct microclimates along it’s north / east and south / west coasts. In our opinion, the south / west of the country along with the central highlands offer the best value for your time, so would recommend going during the dry season in those parts, which runs from December to April.

seasons.title: DECEMBER TO APRIL
editorial: We visited in mid-March, by when the summer was starting to kick in. If temperatures creeping up on mid 30°s isn’t your cup of Ceylon tea, then we recommend visiting during the more pleasant months of December through February.
Needless to say, this is peak tourist season so expect to rub shoulders with fellow travellers.

seasons.title: MAY TO SEPTEMBER
editorial: This is dry season in the north / east, where you can surf the shores of Arugam Bay and the catch the elephant congregation in Minneriya National Park. It is hot hot though, so if that’s not your thing, be forewarned.
The south coast beaches and the central highlands experience heavy rain during this period, so don’t bank on having the best possible experience if you decide to visit.

seasons.title: OCTOBER & NOVEMBER
editorial: This is a strange period with the south / west monsoon receding and north / east monsoon commencing. Expect rains everywhere including the possibility of cyclones, so Sri Lanka is best avoided at this time.
